readout: FANA synthesis rate, normalized to the Tgo-D4K parent (fold)
assay_method: Polymerase kinetic profiling (PKPro). 20 nM polymerase, 1 uM 30-mer DNA template, 100 uM each NTP, 1x ThermoPol buffer, 2x LC Green Plus; denature 95 degC 3 min, extend 55 degC 30 min, fluorescence every 6 s; rate from a linear fit of nucleotides per polymerase vs time; mean of three independent replicates.
remark: No WT row: the readout is already normalized to the Tgo-D4K parent, which is 1.0 by definition. The reference sequence is the engineered Tgo-D4K parent, not native Tgo. Position 659 follows the source data, which carries Y and lists the variant as Y659E; the paper text instead calls it H659E. Q93A is listed twice with values differing by 7e-5, and the mean is used.

protein: RNase III (rnc), the double-stranded RNA endoribonuclease
readout: In vivo dsRNA cleavage, as a log enrichment difference relative to wild type
assay_method: The same site-saturation library transformed into rnc-minus E. coli PH0919 carrying a GFP reporter whose 5-prime UTR stem loop is cleaved by RNase III, sorted by FACS into high and low fluorescence populations. The functional score is the difference in mutation frequency between the two populations relative to wild type, reported as the variance-weighted mean of two replicas.
remark: The reference sequence is the 226-residue rnc coding region printed as the column header of the source matrix, byte-identical to UniProt P0A7Y0. There is no WT row: the source matrix leaves the wild-type residue blank at every position, wild type being the normalizing reference rather than a measured cell. wt_readout is 0 because the score is defined relative to wild type. The 225 nonsense measurements are dropped, a stop codon not being a substitution in this format. The article PDF could not be retrieved and is not redistributed in papers/: PMC serves an HTML interstitial in its place and the publisher returns 403, so only the open supplementary files are staged. As a check on direction, the nuclease-null control E117K reads -2.183 here against the -2.18 the paper prints for it, and the nuclease domain is more sensitive to mutation than the dsRNA-binding domain in all three readouts, as the abstract states. The paper also reports an individually measured growth rate for E117K of 0.71, which is a different measurement from the DMS weighted mean and does not appear here. Not extracted from this paper: the codon-level table of Supplementary Data S8, the per-replica columns, and the k* alignment values of Supplementary Data S10, which are computed rather than assayed.

protein: EfrC, one half of the heterodimeric ABC multidrug efflux pump EfrCD
readout: Variant enrichment under Hoechst 33342 selection, relative to wild type
assay_method: Deep mutational scanning of 41 selected residues of EfrC in the heterodimeric EfrCD pump, by competitive growth of the library under Hoechst 33342 selection with nisin induction. Variant scores were calculated with Enrich2 from three biological replicates.
remark: The reference sequence is UniProt Q837P5 unmodified, against which all 820 mutation labels in the source verify at offset 0. There is no WT row: the source scores are Enrich2 log ratios against wild type, which is 0 by that construction, and the wild-type squares of the scan carry no value at all. The 22 variants for which the source calculated no score, being the squares the paper greys out for high error or sequencing bias, are dropped. readout is the mean of the three replicate scores, all three being present except for 15 variants scored from one or two. The article is paywalled, returns HTML in place of a PDF and is not deposited open access in PMC, so it is not redistributed in papers/; the supplementary workbook it draws on is open and is staged instead. Not extracted from this paper: the no-drug control scan of Extended Data Fig. 2, which the authors use to filter variants rather than as a phenotype; and the cryo-EM structure, nanobody binding and ATPase assays, none of which is a per-variant measurement.
